findings.fix: Remove this rule, or replace it with a rule that doesn't hide `#main-content` in portrait mode (e.g. only adjust layout/spacing, never `display: none`).
findings.violation: This unconditionally hides the entire main content (including the skip-link target) whenever the viewport is in portrait orientation, which includes most phones - the primary way people would read "service announcements" on the go.

findings.fix: Remove `style="outline:none"` or replace it with a custom visible `:focus` style.
findings.violation: `outline:none` removes the visible keyboard-focus indicator with no replacement focus style, making the link unusable for keyboard/screen-reader users to locate - ironic given it's the link to the accessibility page.

findings.evidence: "Commuters can report a service issue by calling rider services. The change takes effect on the following service day."
findings.fix: Replace with actual weekend service details (affected routes, hours, dates), and de-duplicate the repeated "report an issue" boilerplate across sections.
findings.violation: This generic boilerplate doesn't describe any weekend service information and is near-duplicate content of `#s3-p2` ("Riders can report a service issue by calling rider services...") reused under an unrelated heading.

findings.evidence: "Passengers should review the updated schedule through the mobile app. A confirmation message follows once the request is processed."
findings.fix: Rewrite to describe weekend-specific schedule changes, and remove the mismatched "confirmation message" sentence or apply it only where an actual request/submission occurs.
findings.violation: "A confirmation message follows once the request is processed" doesn't logically follow from "review the updated schedule" (reviewing isn't a "request"), and this paragraph is a near-duplicate of `#s3-p1` under a different heading.

findings.evidence: `alt="A newly installed tactile paving strip along the platform edge."`
findings.fix: Move this image to the "Accessibility improvements" section or replace it with an image relevant to weekend service changes.
findings.violation: An image about tactile paving (an accessibility feature) is placed in the "Weekend service" section instead of the "Accessibility improvements" section (`#s3`), where it topically belongs.

findings.evidence: "Riders can check real time arrivals through the online portal. Station staff can also help with the same request in person."
findings.fix: Replace with content describing what schedule changes occurred, or rename the heading to match the real-time-arrivals content.
findings.violation: The heading promises "Schedule changes" but the paragraph only describes checking real-time arrivals, not any actual change to the schedule.

findings.fix: Either show actual before/after schedule changes per zone, or move/rename this table as a "Current status" widget outside the "Schedule changes" section.
findings.violation: A table under "Schedule changes" showing only "On time" for every zone communicates no change at all, contradicting the section heading.

findings.evidence: "Local residents should review the updated schedule through the online portal. A confirmation message follows once the request is processed."
findings.fix: Replace with content actually describing accessibility improvements (e.g., the tactile paving mentioned in `#s1-img1`), and remove the duplicated boilerplate.
findings.violation: This content is about reviewing schedules, not accessibility improvements, and duplicates `#s1-p2` almost verbatim with only nouns swapped.

findings.evidence: "Riders can report a service issue by calling rider services. Station staff can also help with the same request in person."
findings.fix: Replace with accessibility-specific content, or remove this duplicated paragraph.
findings.violation: Duplicate of `#s1-p1`'s topic (reporting issues), unrelated to "Accessibility improvements," suggesting content blocks were copy-pasted across sections without adapting to the heading.

findings.evidence: "Route adjustments take effect on the posted effective date."
findings.fix: State the actual effective date, or link to the page where it is posted.
findings.violation: "the posted effective date" is a vague self-reference with no actual date, and no link or location telling the reader where it is posted.

findings.fix: Remove this element, or only render it after an actual user-initiated save action.
findings.violation: This message implies the user just completed a save action, but nothing on the page (a static announcements page) precedes it with any editable or submittable content - it reads as leftover/placeholder UI text.

findings.fix: Give the button an accessible label or adjacent text clarifying what it refreshes (e.g., "Refresh zone status"), or remove it if non-functional.
findings.violation: The button has no indication of what status it refreshes or what UI it updates, and sits disconnected from any status display it would logically affect.

findings.evidence: `<div class="icon-delete" role="button" tabindex="0" aria-label="Delete item" id="s3-customcontrol" ...>`
findings.fix: Replace with a real `<button>` element (which gets click/keyboard activation for free), and give it a context-specific label (e.g., "Delete saved route") or remove it if it serves no purpose here.
findings.violation: This is a custom `div` with `role="button"` and `tabindex="0"` but no keyboard event handling is present in the markup, so keyboard users can focus it but cannot activate it with Enter/Space; it is also thematically out of place (a generic "Delete item" control with no context) on a transit announcements page.

findings.evidence: `<div class="wizard-steps" id="s3-wizard">` containing "Choose a plan", "Enter payment details", "Confirm your order"
findings.fix: Remove this unrelated wizard block, or if a multi-step flow belongs here, mark it up as an ordered list with `aria-current="step"` on the active step and content relevant to transit accessibility.
findings.violation: This is unrelated e-commerce checkout-flow content embedded in a transit "Accessibility improvements" section, with no semantic list markup and no indication of which step is current.

findings.evidence: "For the full list of upcoming adjustments, check the current station closures."
findings.fix: Make the link text, surrounding sentence, and href all describe the same destination/content (e.g., link text "view upcoming route adjustments" pointing to an adjustments page).
findings.violation: The surrounding text promises "upcoming adjustments," the link text says "station closures," and the href points to `/fares/history` - three different, inconsistent destinations for a single link.

findings.evidence: `<label for="phone" id="s3-form-phone-label">Phone number (required)</label>` paired with `<input id="phone" type="tel" autocomplete="tel">`
findings.violation: "(required)" is conveyed only as visible label text; the input itself has no `required` or `aria-required="true"` attribute, so assistive technology and browser validation won't treat it as required.

findings.evidence: `<input id="promo" type="text" aria-invalid="true">` with error text "Enter a 6 character code using letters and numbers only."
findings.fix: Remove the static `aria-invalid="true"` and set it dynamically only after validation fails.
findings.violation: `aria-invalid="true"` is hardcoded rather than set conditionally after validation, so the field is announced as invalid to screen reader users even before they've typed anything.
The error message span is not associated with the input via `aria-describedby`, so screen reader users focused on the input won't hear the error text.
